# AI

**Last updated:** 2026-10-05 — **Feature:** `src/features/ai/` — coupon and collection forms register as live forms

## Overview

Vendors interact with a streaming AI assistant ("Sidekick") that can answer questions about their shop, query live stats, search and mutate products, collections, and coupons, and hand off to standard dashboard forms pre-filled with suggested values. The feature ships in two forms: a full-page chat at `/store/[shopSlug]/ai` and a slide-in panel (`AiChatPanel`) available anywhere in the dashboard. The rich-text editor's AI actions (improve, shorten, extend, simplify, translate, custom prompt) run through the `aiEditorTransform` GraphQL mutation from `src/shared/lib/editor-ai.ts`.

Each assistant turn renders as an interleaved **work log** (Shopify Sidekick style), not a text bubble followed by a pile of cards. Both surfaces scroll through one shared `Transcript` built on `@repo/ui`'s `MessageScroller`, so following, turn anchoring and the opening position behave the same in each. The back-end streams an ordered `parts[]` list — `{ kind: "text" } | { kind: "tool", event } | { kind: "approval", requests, decisions }` — preserving the exact order the model produced narration and actions in. `AssistantTurn` walks that list: text becomes prose, each tool becomes a humanized `ActionRow` (icon + "Searching products…" → "Found 4 products" + status), the final data-bearing action auto-expands its result card while intermediate lookups stay collapsed, form handoffs render as a prominent CTA card, and the multi-step checklist renders as a single inline card showing the latest snapshot. Legacy turns (persisted before `parts` existed) fall back to `content` + `tool_events`.

## Screens / routes

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/app/store/[shopSlug]/ai/page.tsx` | Full-page Sidekick chat powered by `VendorAgentChat` |
| `src/shared/lib/editor-ai.ts` | The editor's AI actions. Calls `aiEditorTransform` through the Apollo client it gets from `auth/apollo-bridge.ts`. |

The `AiChatPanel` is a sidebar component rendered in the dashboard layout; it is controlled by `useAiChatStore` and is not a separate route. `DashboardShell` keeps the canvas square against the nav (`rounded-ss-none`) and rounds the trailing top corner (`rounded-se-2xl`) — the outer edge when the panel is closed, the gap beside Sidekick when it is open.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Vendor types message] --> B[VendorAgentChat / AiChatPanel]
    B --> C[useVendorAgent hook]
    C -->|POST SSE| D[/vendor-agent/chat/stream]
    D -->|text_delta events| C
    D -->|tool_start / tool_progress / tool_result events| C
    D -->|done event| C
    D -->|approval_required event| P[ApprovalCard: Approve / Reject]
    P -->|POST decisions| Q[/vendor-agent/chat/resume/stream]
    Q -->|resumes the same turn| C
    C -->|ordered parts[] built live| E[streaming state painted live]
    E --> N[AssistantTurn work log]
    N --> R[ActionRow humanized rows]
    R --> F[ToolEventRenderer]
    F --> G{Tool name}
    G -->|navigate_to_form| H[NavigateToFormCard button: stash ticket + navigateGuarded]
    G -->|form_patch| O[FormPatchCard; patch staged into the live form]
    G -->|list_collections etc.| I[Typed tool card in ResultCardShell]
    C -->|conversation_id| J[localStorage persistence]
    K[ConversationsSidebar] -->|GraphQL| L[vendorAgentConversations query]
    K -->|switchConversation| C
```

## State & forms

Two Zustand stores: `useAiChatStore` (`store-chat.ts`) manages panel open/closed/expanded state and a `pendingPrompt` queue; `useVendorAgentPrefillStore` (`store-prefill.ts`) persists one **handoff ticket** per target in `sessionStorage` (15 min TTL) for product, collection and coupon forms to consume after a `navigate_to_form` tool event. A ticket carries everything the save on the other side needs — `handoffId`, `values`, `nextStep`, `placeStockAt` — because a form-handoff tool returns them as siblings and splitting them across stores is what let them get out of step. The form reads it with a non-destructive `peek` (strict mode double-mounts); `takeHandoff(target, entityId?)` consumes it on save, and `useVendorAgentPrefill` (or `useVendorAgentHandoff`, the same read returning the whole ticket, which the product form uses for its `handoffId`) releases it when the vendor leaves the form unsaved, so a rejected draft cannot reappear inside the TTL. Targets: `product_create`, `product_edit`, `collection_create`, `coupon_create`, `coupon_edit`. The four per-type coupon forms read it via `useVendorAgentPrefill("coupon_create"|"coupon_edit", couponId)` merged into `defaultValues`; the coupon `create_coupon`/`update_coupon` tools emit form-field values in **major units** and the form converts to cents/bps on submit.

**No save bar:** the AI feature has no editing screens of its own; no react-hook-form forms and no contextual save bar. The `stashPrefill` helper writes to the prefill store before the router navigates to a form page in another feature.

**The live form channel (2026-10-01; coupon and collection forms register the same way).** Coupon create and edit (`useCouponLiveForm` on all four coupon forms) and collection create (`useLiveForm` on the create screen, not the edit screen and not the product-form drawer) register under their own handoff, and `NavigateToFormCard` refuses a second ticket when that form is the one on screen. "لأ، خلي السعر 300" used to be impossible: the form reads its prefill once at mount, a second card pushes the URL already on screen (no remount), and `send()` carried no form state. Now a product form opened from a handoff registers itself in `useLiveFormStore` (`store-live-form.ts`, not persisted) through `useLiveForm` (`lib/live-form.ts`) under its ticket's `handoffId`, for as long as it is mounted. `send()` and `regenerate()` read `currentLiveForm()` at send time and add `form: { form_id, target, entity_id?, values }` to the SSE body — only while the ticket is still the pending one (read from `pending` directly, so it outlives the 15-minute TTL while the form is on screen; it ends on save, on leaving the form, or when a newer card replaces the ticket). `values` is `productSnapshot`: the allow-list mirrored from the back-end, typed numbers as numbers, the description as capped plain text, empty fields left out. A `tool_result` whose `result` carries `form_patch` goes through `applyFormPatchFromResult`: when its `form_id` and `target` match the live form it calls the form's `apply` (`applyPatchToForm`: `setValue(..., { shouldDirty: true })` per field, a one-locale translatable merged over the current value, a `null` — `patch_form`'s `clear`, "شيل الخصم" — written as that field's own blank from `CLEARED_VALUE` (numbers as `null` rather than `undefined`, which the ticket's JSON would drop and a reload would then undo; a `null` for a field with no blank is ignored), then `trigger`), so the fields turn dirty and the save bar shows — nothing is saved — and the ticket's `values` are re-stashed with a fresh TTL so a reload reopens the draft as patched; otherwise the patch is dropped. Either outcome is recorded by `patch_id`, which the card reads. Only live frames apply: a reloaded thread never re-applies an old patch. An API without the channel ignores `form` and never sends a patch, so a form then behaves exactly as before.

**Three edges of the handoff (2026-10-02).** *The refusal the assistant corrects itself.* `create_product` / `update_product` decline a second card for the form already open (`AGENT_FORM_ALREADY_OPEN`), and the next row is usually the `patch_form` card that did the job — so `ActionRow` draws that one refusal as a quiet grey row ("The form is already open on your screen", an info dot) rather than the red "Operation failed" card, through `isFormAlreadyOpenRefusal` (`lib/live-form.ts`): a refusal whose `code` is `AGENT_FORM_ALREADY_OPEN` (2026-10-04: the back-end's `toolRejection` sends the i18n key as `code`, and when a refusal has one it is the whole answer). A turn persisted before that has no code, so for those it falls back to `ok: false` from one of the two tools whose `hint` names `patch_form`, which no other refusal of theirs did. Every other failure stays red. *An old handoff card for the form on screen.* `NavigateToFormCard` used to stash a new ticket and push the URL the vendor was already on: no remount, so the new ticket only replaced the one the form was registered under — the live channel ended, the mounted form's save ran the card's `nextStep` / `placeStockAt` / receipt, and a dirty form put up the leave dialog for the page it was on. Now, when `isLiveFormFor(target, entityId)` says the assistant's form for that target (and, on an edit, that product) is mounted and the card's URL is the current `pathname`, the click stashes nothing, navigates nowhere and shows "This form is already open on your screen…" under the button; a card for a different product, or pressed once the form has unmounted, opens as before. *`regenerate()` could silently no-op.* Its `removed` flag was set inside the `setMessages` updater and read straight after the call, which holds only while React computes the update eagerly; with another update to the hook already queued in the same tick (a save receipt landing as Retry is pressed) the updater was deferred and Retry did nothing. It now decides from the render's own `messages` — last turn an assistant's, or return — and removes that turn by id, so a row appended meanwhile is not the one dropped. `use-vendor-agent.test.tsx` pins the deferred case.

**The composer chip (2026-10-04).** While that live form is on screen the panel's composer shows a small chip above the attachments row: "Editing: <product title>" on an edit form, "New product" on a create form, with "Sidekick can see this form and change it for you. Nothing is saved until you press Save." as its tooltip and screen-reader text. `useLiveFormChip()` (`lib/live-form.ts`) is `currentLiveForm`'s condition as a subscription — a registered form whose ticket is still the pending one — so the chip appears when the assistant's form mounts and goes when it unmounts, is saved, or loses its ticket to a newer card; a form the vendor opened themselves never registers and shows none. The title is the registration's `label`: the product's **saved** title in the dashboard's language (`titleIn`), which `ProductForm` passes to `useLiveForm` on an edit — not the name field's current text, so a rename still unsaved does not change what the chip calls the product. `LiveFormChip` (`components/live-form-chip.tsx`) is presentational and wraps the title in `<bdi>`, so an English title inside the Arabic sentence keeps its own direction. Only `ai-chat-panel.tsx` renders it: the full-page `/ai` chat is never on screen beside a product form.

**Multi-step requests (dynamic, any tasks):** two mechanisms cover "do X then Y then Z" in one message.
- *Chained auto-resume across form saves.* Every form-handoff tool (`create_product`/`create_collection`/`create_coupon`/`update_product`/`update_coupon`) can return a `next_step` string in its `navigate_to_form`. `NavigateToFormCard` stashes it on the handoff ticket. On save success each submit hook (`use-product-submit`, `use-collection-editor`, `use-coupon-submit`) consumes the ticket with `takeHandoff` and passes it to `resumeAgentAfterSave(handoff, marker)` (`store-followup.ts`), which `openWithPrompt`s `\`${nextStep} ${marker}\`` where `marker` is `[product:ID]` / `[collection:ID]` (empty for coupons). The panel (in the dashboard shell, survives navigation) auto-sends, so the agent runs the next step against the just-saved entity with no "continue". A step reaches a save only if that save is the one it was staged for: the step used to sit in one global slot, so a collection or coupon **edit** — direct writes with no form handoff, which can never queue a step — could consume the step queued for a different, still-unsaved entity. The collection-edit call site is gone for that reason. An assisted save lands the vendor on the entity it just created rather than on the list.
- *Progress checklist.* The `set_task_plan` tool echoes an ordered step list (`{title, status: pending|active|done}`). The agent re-sends the COMPLETE list after every step — **including across turns**, because the chained flow above auto-resumes as a new turn — so `lib/task-plan.ts` reads the plan as **conversation state**: `latestPlan(messages)` finds the newest snapshot anywhere in the thread and only that turn draws the card (`planIsCurrent`), while `AssistantTurn` still takes the last re-send within its own `parts`. Deduping per turn was all a turn could do and was not enough: the canonical two-step request ended as two frozen To-do cards, the older one still spinning. A finished turn with an `active` step renders it as **waiting on you** rather than a spinner — a form-handoff turn ends precisely because it is waiting, so the never-ending spinner was the normal case. `TaskPlanStrip` pins a one-line "step 2 of 3 · <title>" above the composer while a plan is incomplete: the panel lives in `DashboardShell` and travels with the vendor to the form, but the transcript does not follow them, and the card was scrolled up inside it. Everything is derived from the message list rather than a store, so the public share view gets the same reading. The prompt's rule is that a step finishes when its work is done — for a form handoff, when the save auto-resumes the agent, **not** when it calls the tool; it used to mark a coupon step `done` immediately after `create_coupon`, which creates nothing, so the card read 2/2 with the coupon form still empty.

**The save receipt.** When the vendor saves something the agent prepared, `useSaveReceipt` calls `vendorAgentSaveReceipt` and the server writes an assistant turn recording it — **no model call**: every agent turn bills the shop's plan allowance, and a sentence that is always the same shape must not pay for a generation, be slower than the save it acknowledges, or be able to fail on an overloaded provider. It is persisted rather than drawn locally so it does both halves of what was asked: the vendor sees it, and the model sees it whenever the thread is next loaded. Scope is the handoff ticket: only a save that completed one gets a receipt, never a save the vendor made on their own, and never when the ticket carried a `next_step` — the chained resume is already about to speak, and two messages about one save read as two saves. The ticket also carries the `conversationId` captured at click time, because by save time the vendor may be on a different thread. The row arrives through `useAiChatStore.pendingReceipt` and is appended by whichever surface is mounted on that conversation; it deliberately does **not** open the panel, since the vendor is standing on a form they just saved. `SaveReceiptCard` renders the way back to the record, which the sentence cannot carry — the work-log renderer drops links from assistant text on purpose.

**Approvals (human-in-the-loop):** the back-end graph suspends before any of five bulk/irreversible writes and emits a terminal `approval_required` event. `useVendorAgent` commits the paused turn as a normal message — narration plus an `approval` part with empty `decisions` — and exposes `pendingApproval`. `ApprovalCard` renders live buttons only on the turn the server is actually parked on (`pendingApproval && m.id === messages.at(-1)?.id`); every other approval card in the transcript is read-only history. `resolveApproval(decisions)` POSTs to `/vendor-agent/chat/resume/stream` and streams the rest of that turn with `replaceLast: true`, because the resumed run returns the **whole** turn (its `parts` span the pause) — appending would duplicate the narration and the card. A thread reopened mid-approval restores the live card by scanning the last message for an `approval` part with no decisions, so a vendor can close the tab and finish later.

**Streaming state:** `useVendorAgent` maintains local React state (`messages`, `streaming`, `sending`, `conversationId`, `pendingApproval`). As SSE events arrive it builds an ordered `parts[]` the same way the back-end does — flushing buffered text into a text part before each tool batch, mutating the pending tool event in place on `tool_result` (one object reference shared with `tool_events`) — so the in-progress turn already reads as a work log. On `done` it prefers the server's authoritative `parts`. A failed turn is not a banner: the hook appends an `{ kind: "error", code, message, retryable }` part to whatever the turn already produced and commits it, so the narration and tool rows that preceded the failure survive, a reload shows what the live session showed, and **Try again** has a turn to rewind to. A socket that closes with neither `done` nor `error` gets the same treatment under `STREAM_CLOSED` rather than being presented as a finished reply. Apollo is not used for chat; history hydration uses a single `useLazyQuery` (`VENDOR_AGENT_CONVERSATION`, which now selects `parts`).

**Response rendering:** a single `AssistantTurn` renders both committed and streaming assistant turns across the full-page chat, the slide-in panel, and the read-only shared view — so the work-log presentation is identical everywhere. `humanize-tool.ts` maps each tool name (+ args/result) to a localized icon, a present-tense running label, a resolved done label, and a past-tense failed label (a red row used to keep the running one and read as still in progress).

**Text parts render a small markdown subset** through `lib/light-markdown.tsx` — `**bold**`, `` `code` `` and simple `-`/`1.` lists become real markup; headings and table pipes are stripped to their text; fence markers are dropped; **links are never rendered**, so an assistant-authored href cannot become a phishing surface. There is no parser dependency and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`: every leaf goes through React as a string. The system prompt still asks for plain text, but the free-tier models the platform falls back to emit markdown regardless, and the vendor was reading the raw asterisks. Chat channels (WhatsApp/Telegram) stay plain — they have no renderer.

`AssistantTurn` also folds a lookup the model repeated with identical arguments into one row badged `×2`; failed calls never fold, so an error and its retry both stay visible.

## GraphQL operations

| Operation | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `VendorAgentBriefing` | Query | Today's revenue, orders, low-stock, new-customer snapshot shown on the empty-state briefing card. Revenue as `revenue_today_cents`/`revenue_total_cents` (integer cents since 2026-09-12) |
| `VendorAgentWeeklyInsights` | Query | The last 7 complete shop-local days (today is the briefing's) vs the 7 before, with 14 daily points that sum to the headline. Revenue as `revenue_7d_cents`/`revenue_prior_7d_cents`/`daily.revenue_cents` (integer cents since 2026-09-12) |
| `VendorAgentConversations` | Query | List active conversations (with optional search) for the sidebar |
| `VendorAgentArchivedConversations` | Query | List archived conversations shown in the sidebar archive tab |
| `VendorAgentConversation` | Query | Load full message history for a specific conversation (used when hydrating from localStorage or switching) |
| `PublicVendorAgentConversationByToken` | Query | Fetch a shared conversation by its public token |
| `VendorAgentChat` | Mutation | Non-streaming fallback (superseded by SSE endpoint in normal use) |
| `DeleteVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Delete a single conversation |
| `PinVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Pin or unpin a conversation |
| `RenameVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Rename a conversation title |
| `BulkDeleteVendorAgentConversations` | Mutation | Delete multiple conversations at once |
| `BulkPinVendorAgentConversations` | Mutation | Pin or unpin multiple conversations |
| `ShareVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Generate a public share token with optional TTL and PIN |
| `UnlockSharedVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Unlock a PIN-protected shared conversation. Selects `parts` like the public lookup (since 2026-10-01; without it a PIN-protected share fell back to all text, then all tool rows, and lost approval and error parts) |
| `RevokeVendorAgentConversationShare` | Mutation | Revoke an existing share token |
| `RestoreVendorAgentConversation` | Mutation | Restore an archived conversation |

## Validation

None. Chat input is a plain textarea with no Zod schema; the editor route validates source text and action with plain TypeScript guards.

## Main files

- `src/features/ai/lib/use-vendor-agent.ts` — core SSE streaming hook; owns all chat state, builds the live ordered `parts[]`, and the stream/regenerate/resolveApproval/stop/reset/switchConversation lifecycle
- `src/features/ai/components/assistant-turn.tsx` — the work-log renderer shared by the chat, panel, and shared view
- `src/features/ai/components/transcript.tsx` — the shared scroll surface (following, turn anchoring, opening position, jump-to-latest, log semantics)
- `src/features/ai/lib/light-markdown.tsx` — the bounded markdown subset a reply may carry, with no dependency and no raw HTML
- `src/features/ai/components/tool-cards/approval-card.tsx` — the Approve/Reject gate for the back-end's five gated writes; read-only once decided
- `src/features/ai/lib/humanize-tool.ts` — tool name → localized icon + running/done action labels, and `humanizeProgress`, the phase → sentence table behind a running tool's progress line
- `src/features/ai/store-chat.ts` — Zustand store controlling the slide-in panel visibility and pending-prompt queue
- `src/features/ai/store-prefill.ts` — sessionStorage-backed Zustand store for handing off AI-suggested field values to create/edit forms; `store-live-form.ts` + `lib/live-form.ts` — the live form channel (which form is mounted, its snapshot, applying a `patch_form` result)
- `src/features/ai/store-followup.ts` — sessionStorage-backed Zustand store holding the pending "next step" for a chained request; consumed on product-create success to auto-resume the chat
- `src/features/ai/components/vendor-agent-chat.tsx` — full-page chat component with voice input, image upload, @-mentions, in-conversation find bar, and export
- `src/features/ai/components/ai-chat-panel.tsx` — resizable sidebar panel variant of the chat
- `src/features/ai/lib/inline-mentions.ts` — the panel's inline mention model: segmenting a draft into plain and mention runs, splicing a pick into the text, rebuilding the `[Referenced: …]` tail from the text, and splitting a sent message into highlighted runs plus leftover pills
- `src/features/ai/components/conversation-search-dialog.tsx` — command-palette popup to search past conversations / start a new one from the panel header
- `src/features/ai/components/tool-cards/tool-event-renderer.tsx` — dispatches each `tool_event` to the correct typed result card
- `src/shared/lib/editor-ai.ts` — the editor's AI actions, and the bridge they reach the Apollo client through

## Notes

- **All copy reads `aiChat.*` (en + ar), never an inline `isAr ? … : …` pair.** `isAr` is left only where it drives layout (`dir`, the sheet's side, chevrons), a locale argument (date/number formatting, `name[locale]` on bilingual records, the voice language), or text sent to the model as the vendor's own message — starter and quick-action prompts, `lib/suggest-follow-ups.ts`, the briefing tiles, the weekly Analyze — which stays an EN/AR pair in code. The send button's accessible name reads Stop while a reply streams. `tool-cards/labels.ts` turns raw status/type values (`PUBLISH`, `SIMPLE`, `at_local_facility`) into labels; a value it has no message for renders as it used to (lowercased, underscores spaced). Tests that assert Arabic use `test-utils/next-intl.ts` (`bilingualNextIntlMock`, `setTestLocale`).
- **Three refusals, not one (2026-09-12).** The back-end used to answer every ceiling with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, so `TurnErrorCard` could only say one thing about three different problems. It now reads three codes apart. `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` is the **shop's plan allowance** — the one refusal a vendor can act on, so it is the only one with a way out: `planHref` is threaded `AiChatPanel` → `MessageBubble` → `AssistantTurn` → the card, built as `/store/${activeShopSlug}/settings/plan` from `useActiveShopStore`. The panel is the only surface that supplies it today; the prop is optional, so the full-page chat and the read-only shared view (whose reader owns no shop to upgrade) render the same card without the **View plan** button. `PLATFORM_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` is the **platform's own** spending cap, so it joins the `PROVIDER_*`/`MODEL_NOT_FOUND`/`NOT_CONFIGURED` group that says the team has been notified and offers nothing to press. `RATE_LIMITED` is this user's own hourly bucket — "The limit clears on its own within the hour", no button (the back-end sends it `retryable: false`) and deliberately no "team notified", because nothing is wrong. An unrecognised code still lands on the generic "The reply didn't finish" card, so a back-end that only sends `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` keeps working. `tool-cards/turn-error-card.render.test.tsx` pins the three apart, plus the fallback and the missing-`planHref` case.
- **A running tool now says how far it has got (2026-09-12).** `tool_progress` frames arrive between a tool's `tool_start` and its `tool_result` and land on that row's `event.progress`; `ActionRow` swaps the tool's present-tense label for the phase's ("Checking rows"), adds a `120 / 500` count, a thin bar, and the handle the server quoted. Three things it deliberately does not do. It **draws no bar without a fraction** — `generate_product_image` can only name its phase, and a bar with an invented value is worse than none. It **keeps the plain running orb** for a tool that emits nothing, which is every tool but three. And it **matches on `call_id`**, not on tool name: one model turn can call the same tool twice, and `findPendingTool` binding by name put the second call's progress — and then its result — on the first call's row. An unknown `phase` is not an error, it falls back to the tool's own label, so the back-end can name a new stage without a dashboard release. Nothing here is persisted: a reloaded conversation has no progress because every row in it is finished.
- **The shop's currency is read, not assumed.** `useShopCurrency` (`src/shared/hooks/use-shop-currency.ts`) resolves it from the `MyShops` cache for the active slug. The panel and the shared view used to pass a literal `"USD"` to every result card and the `/ai` route passed one too, so a SAR shop's assistant quoted dollars. The shared view has no shop context at all, so its share payload names the shop's own: `PublicVendorAgentConversationByToken` and `UnlockSharedVendorAgentConversation` select `conversation { currency }` (2026-10-04), and `sharedConversationCurrency` (`lib/conversation-currency.ts`) prices every card in it. When the payload names none it takes the one the thread itself recorded (`conversationCurrency`: the latest `get_shop_stats` / `get_custom_range_stats` result, which echoes `Shop.currency`), then the platform default; a value that is not an ISO code is skipped. **An API built before the field refuses the whole operation**, and this app deploys first, so `lib/legacy-share-currency.ts` (transitional) holds each document as it was before the field and the two hooks the view uses: `useSharedConversationLookup` runs the legacy query when the current one fails for an unknown field (`isUnknownFieldError`, `shared/lib/apollo/legacy-fallback.ts`, shared with the auth code-length fallback) and stays loading until that retry answers, and `useUnlockSharedConversation` does the same for the PIN unlock - safe to repeat, since a request refused at validation never ran. Pinned by `shared-conversation-view.render.test.tsx`.
- **Two money units in this feature, and the split is deliberate.** The two GraphQL queries return **integer cents** (`revenue_today_cents`, `revenue_total_cents`, `revenue_7d_cents`, `revenue_prior_7d_cents`, `daily.revenue_cents`), so `daily-briefing-card.tsx` and `weekly-insights-card.tsx` each scale once in their own `formatMoneyCents` helper and nowhere else. The **tool result cards** (`tool-cards/shop-stats-card.tsx`, `tool-cards/custom-range-stats-card.tsx`, `tool-cards/top-products-card.tsx`, `tool-cards/yearly-sales-card.tsx`) read the agent's tool JSON, not GraphQL, and that payload is **major units** — the back-end tool applies `fromCents` before handing the number to the model, which writes prose with a currency symbol and has no formatter. So `result.total_revenue` / `p.total_sales` on those cards are correct as plain `formatMoney` calls (the two stats cards share the one in `tool-cards/stats-format.ts`); converting them would be a 100x bug.
- **The two sales-stats cards read two payload shapes (2026-09-29).** `get_shop_stats` and `get_custom_range_stats` now return `version: 2`, and every conversation persisted before that — plus every turn answered by an API not yet rebuilt — still holds v1, so `ShopStatsResult` and `CustomRangeStatsResult` in `lib/types.ts` are unions split by `isShopStatsV2` / `isCustomRangeStatsV2`. The renderer still routes on `"revenue" in result` and on `"range"` + `"total_revenue"`, keys both versions carry, and the card picks the layout. **v2** puts the real window in the header ("Last 7 days" with the shop-local dates, formatted as calendar days in UTC with Latin digits), and every tile covers it: sales (net of returns, shown under it when non-zero), orders counted as sales ("of 16 placed" when cancelled or failed ones were left out), average order and new customers. Below them, `ChannelBreakdown` draws `by_channel` as a thin stacked bar plus one legend row per channel, taking icon, colour and name from `@/shared/lib/sales-channels` and the `salesChannels` namespace so a channel looks the same here as on the analytics page; an unknown channel renders neutral under the server's spelling. The small print gives lifetime sales and orders and our own translation of the sales basis, with the server's English `sales_basis` as its hover title. **v1** is where "this week's sales" was read off a lifetime completed-only total under a "This week" badge, so a v1 card drops the badge, names each tile's real scope ("Lifetime revenue", "Lifetime orders", "New customers (30 days)"), carries the period on the status chips alone, and says its revenue counted completed orders only. After `get_shop_stats`, `lib/suggest-follow-ups.ts` offers a comparison with the window before the one shown ("Compare with the 7 days before") rather than a fixed "last month".
- Chat responses stream over REST SSE endpoints (`POST /vendor-agent/chat/{stream,regenerate/stream,resume/stream}`), not GraphQL. Apollo is only used for conversation history queries and sidebar mutations.
- A request ends on either `done` or `approval_required`. The latter is not an error — the back-end graph is suspended on its checkpoint and resumes only when a decision reaches `chat/resume/stream`. Abandoning it is safe: the next message on that conversation declines it server-side, so nothing gated runs.
- The `navigate_to_form` tool result is shape-driven (presence of the `navigate_to_form` key), not name-driven, so any tool can trigger a form prefill handoff. So is `form_patch`, and `AssistantTurn` treats both as prominent cards outside repeat-folding and auto-expand: two corrections to one price are two things that happened.
- The last-active `conversation_id` is persisted in `localStorage` keyed by `vendor_agent_conv:<shopSlug>` and rehydrated on mount.
- **Attached images ride two channels.** On send, **both** composers (`vendor-agent-chat.tsx` and `ai-chat-panel.tsx`) append the `[Attached images: …]` text marker (for the LLM's context and reload display) **and** pass the uploads as a structured `attachments[]` on the SSE body via `send(text, attachments)`. The backend feeds that structured array to `create_product`/`update_product`, so attached photos land on the product form deterministically — no reliance on the model copying URLs. Create → first image is primary, rest fill the gallery; edit → appended to the product's existing media. Both composers strip the marker off the sent user bubble and re-render the attached images as thumbnails, so what the vendor sent stays visible in the transcript.
- **The editor's AI actions moved to the API (2026-09-07), and the reason was governance, not behaviour.** They ran in `src/app/api/ai/editor/route.ts`, a Next.js route calling Groq directly with a `GROQ_API_KEY` from this app's own environment. That route is deleted. What it did not do, and `aiEditorTransform` now does: check a session, book a plan quota, apply the per-user rate limit and the platform's daily budget, moderate the output, record the spend in `usage_events` so it reaches the admin's cost screen, and honour the provider an admin picks at `/integrations/ai-chat` — switching the platform to OpenRouter used to leave the editor on Groq, silently. The HTML sanitiser (fences, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<html>`/`<body>`, inline `on*`) moved with it; on the client it was the only thing between a provider's response and the dashboard's own origin.
- **The seven buttons bill four different capability keys** — `ai.text.rewrite` (improve / extend / simplify), `ai.text.summarize` (shorten), `ai.text.translate` (both translations), `ai.text.generate` (custom prompt) — charged per character. `ai.text.rewrite` is `false` on FREE, so Improve and Extend fail on that tier while Translate still works. Three of those keys were priced in the plan matrix and read by no code before this.
- **`runAiEditorAction` keeps its signature, and that is deliberate.** Its callers (`tiptap-ui/ai-menu.tsx`, `tiptap-ui/ai-ask-button.tsx`) are upstream Tiptap scaffold on the eslint exemption list — we do not maintain them and the next sync overwrites local edits. So the Apollo client arrives through `shared/lib/auth/apollo-bridge.ts` (the same bridge `clearApolloCache` already used) rather than as a new argument. `getApolloClient()` returns null before `TokenRefreshProvider` mounts, and the function throws a retryable message rather than asserting.
- Every waiting state in the feature — "Thinking…" while a turn is in flight, "Processing…" inside the panel's streaming bubble, "Generating…" on the image-generation card, and both "Loading conversation…" placeholders — renders through `ShiningText` (`@repo/ui/components/shining-text`), a highlight sweeping across the text. Its gradient is built from the `--muted-foreground` / `--foreground` tokens so it works in light and dark, and it falls back to plain muted text under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Each call site carries `role="status" aria-live="polite"`. The agent chat’s "Thinking…" and every running `ActionRow` also draw `AgentOrb` (`components/agent-orb.tsx`), a 20px `ThinkingOrb` from the `thinking-orbs` package tinted the work log’s violet, in place of the old spinner. The row picks the animation from the tool’s verb prefix (`orbStateForTool`: lookups search, content generators compose, writes work). It is `aria-hidden` because the orb’s own label is English-only and the text beside it already says what is happening, and its colour is a hex literal because the orb parses only `#hex` / `rgb()`.
- **`@`-mentions have two models, and the split is per surface.** Both open the same hierarchical picker — categories (Products, Collections, Orders, Customers, Coupons), then that category's entities, with products and coupons searching server-side (`search` arg) while collections, orders and customers fetch one page and filter client-side — and both send the same `[Referenced: type:id "display"; …]` tail, mirroring the `[Attached images: …]` convention so the agent can resolve an entity by id. What differs is where a picked entity goes.
  - **The full-page chat keeps the chip model.** `lib/use-mention-composer.ts` lifts the entity *out* of the textarea and shows it as a removable chip above the input; the picker (`mention-dropdown.tsx`) floats full-width above the composer. The picked list is the truth, and `serializeMentions` reads it directly. The hook abstracts the textarea behind `getValue`/`setValue`, which is what lets it drive that composer's uncontrolled `ref` textarea.
  - **The slide-in panel is inline (2026-09-13).** The entity stays in the draft as `@Display`, painted by a mirrored backdrop (`mention-textarea.tsx`), and the picker opens at the "@" (`inline-mention-menu.tsx`). Because the text is now the truth, `lib/use-inline-mention-composer.ts` keeps `resolved` only as a *lookup* and the tail is **rebuilt by scanning the draft on every send** (`serializeInlineMentions`) — so a token the vendor deleted with Backspace is simply absent, with nothing tracking the deletion. That hook is panel-only and takes `value`/`setValue` rather than the getter pair, because a backdrop can only mirror a value React actually renders.
- **Going inline forced a matching change to the sent bubble, and it is the non-obvious half.** Both bubbles render the stripped text and then every `[Referenced: …]` entry as a pill underneath, so an inline token would have shown the product name twice — once as flat text in the bubble, once as a chip below it — and the highlight the vendor watched light up in the composer would vanish on send. `splitBubbleMentions` answers both at once: a tagged mention found in the text is highlighted in place, and only the ones with nothing to highlight fall through to pills. One pass therefore covers a panel message (all inline, no pills), a full-page-chat message and any turn persisted before this change (nothing inline, all pills).
- **The token boundary is not the reference implementation's.** `lib/inline-mentions.ts` matches a token at a word boundary spelled out as a character class rather than with `(?=$|[^\w])`: JavaScript's `\w` is ASCII-only, so the obvious lookahead treats every Arabic letter as a boundary and matches `@هودي` inside `@هوديات`. Forms are also matched longest-first, so a shop holding both "Hoodie" and "Hoodie Winter" resolves the longer one. `inline-mentions.spec.ts` pins both, and an English-only fixture set would catch neither.
- **The trigger is re-derived from the live caret, not only from `change`.** `MentionTextarea` binds `onClick` and `onKeyUp` as well as `onChange`, because a caret that moves without typing — a click back into a token, an arrow key out of one — fires no change event, and a picker that only listens to `change` is then stale in both directions. It also closes on blur after 120ms (rows pick on `mousedown`, so they never take focus). Without that close, the picker stayed parked on a drilled-in category while the vendor reached for the `+` menu again, and the **Mention** item then wrote an `@` while changing nothing the popup renders from — so the command read as dead until an edit reset it. That item is therefore `openAtCaret`, a command that always reopens at the root, deliberately **not** routed through `onValueChange`: the typing path keeps the drilled-in category on purpose, and a command is not a keystroke.
- **Clicking a mention that is already resolved opens its own list, not the category menu.** The two look like the same event and need opposite answers: a caret inside a half-typed `@cou` is a vendor choosing a *kind*, while a caret inside `@SALE20` is one whose kind is already settled and who only wants to swap the entity. `mentionSpanAt` separates them, and returns the token's span as well — so the swap replaces the **whole** token rather than the half before the caret, which would otherwise leave `@SALE20` as `@WELCOME20`. The same check makes `collapseToken` refuse a resolved run, so Back and Escape close instead of rewriting the token and eating part of the entity.
- **A category that matched nothing hands Enter back.** `onKeyDown` returns `false` when there is no row to pick, so the composer's own Enter-to-send still works; swallowing it left a vendor looking at "No matches" unable to send the message they had already typed.
- **`lib/use-mention-search.ts` clears its debounce immediately (2026-09-13).** Drilling into a category resets the query to `""`, and a 180ms lag there meant the category's *first* request went out filtered by the token typed before the click. The back-end matches a coupon `search` against the code alone, so `@cou` returned nothing and a shop full of coupons read as empty. The clear is adjusted during render; only typing is debounced. The same pass made `loading` honest — `useLazyQuery` reports `loading: false` before `execute()` runs, and the two `useQuery` categories never reported it at all, so the picker painted "No matches" in the gap before it had even asked — and surfaced `error`, since Apollo blanks `data` on failure and an unreachable API was indistinguishable from an empty shop.
- **Two mechanics in the panel's composer look arbitrary and are not.** The picker's anchor is measured from the composer's **top** edge even though the popup opens upwards (`lib/caret-anchor.ts`): the composer grows downwards from a fixed top as the textarea auto-grows, so a distance from its bottom is stale for exactly the keystroke that both wraps a line and types the `@`, and the popup lands over the token it is filtering. And a splice that does not change the string — picking a category from a bare `@` collapses `@` to `@`, which is the ordinary flow — applies the caret **immediately** instead of queueing it, because React bails out of an identical `setState` and the layout effect keyed on the value never runs; a queued caret would then sit armed and land in front of the next character typed. `use-inline-mention-composer.test.tsx` pins both. The caret is also read from the marker's **inline-start** edge, which is its right under `direction: rtl`.
- **The composer's focus ring and token flash are CSS, not `motion`** — an appended, deliberately unlayered block at the foot of `src/app/globals.css`. Both animate a decoration no React state needs to know about, and a spring on a ring that only turns while the textarea has focus would cost a re-render a frame. Every name is prefixed `compose-`, because `siri-orb` already declares a global `@property --angle` and `@keyframes rotate` from its own inline `<style>` and the panel mounts that component twice. The ring replaces the pill's old static `focus-within:ring` rather than joining it; two rings at two radii read as a mistake.
